You said there was another incident where it kind of got a little comical

after 119L, they were reconnaissance cameras for, you know, for satellites, reconnaissance

but it was with a 10,000-pound payload, and it was classified as usual,
but to the extent where they flew, in addition to our tracking crew,
crew. They had a crew specialist in helicopters, as I remember, that went along. So they would

the whole fleet.
Security personnel?
Yeah, security personnel.
Armed security personnel?

that Holman Department area as possible,
in order to, because there was a maximum amount of optical targets down there,
you know, a million houses and so on.
and I had good luck in hitting the target pretty much square.
So we spent quite a bit of time on the outskirts of Dallas
at 100,000 feet getting data.

where that's where the ejector would carry us away from the city we didn't want to be near any

it, it was on a Sunday, and Dallas was playing at home, so everybody was tuned to it. No,
it couldn't have been home, because it would be a blackout. Anyway, Dallas was playing
on a Sunday, so everybody in Dallas was tuned to the TV set.
When the thing came down, the streets were pretty empty,
and so the guys were able to kind of wrap things up
with not too many people around.
And then as they were finishing wrapping it up, the game ended,
and everybody kept pouring into the streets.

so it wasn't any problem.
They just told them it was an Air Force experiment,
and they were working to get the thing secured and so on. So they had a black block party and

flying in from Bedford. They were changing planes to Dallas and they expected this, you
know, if there was a recovery, to be on the bond dock someplace. Instead, they saw this
triple-shoot system with 10,000 pounds come floating down right within sight of the airport
board where they shook up.
